title: China Warns of 'Consequences' Over Taiwan's Pacific Islands Forum Presence
detail: China's ambassador to the Pacific nations, Qian Bo, said on September 1, 2026 that Beijing had "serious concerns" about the space given to Taiwan at the Pacific Islands Forum in Palau, telling reporters "Taiwan is not a dialogue partner with the forum so we have serious concerns." Asked whether there would be consequences for Taiwan's participation, Qian said, "There will always be consequences ... this should not have happened. We think it's very inappropriate," while stating this was not a threat but a sovereign state's expression of concern. The exchange came a day after Taiwan Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung and a Taiwanese business delegation attended the forum's opening ceremony in Palau, one of Taipei's three remaining diplomatic allies in the Pacific.

title: MND's Annual China Military Power Report Flags Accelerating PLA Island-Landing Preparations
detail: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense submitted its 2026 report on China's military power to the Legislative Yuan on September 1, 2026. The report identifies joint island-landing capability as a PLA force-development priority, citing upgraded Z-20 utility helicopters, new Type 076 amphibious assault ships, and advanced landing barges built to address existing equipment shortcomings, alongside enhancements in military space operations, cyberspace warfare, AI-based deepfake technology, and battlefield medical logistics. The report assesses that current PLA landing-operation capabilities remain inadequate, with most programs not expected to mature until 2030-2035. Analyst Chieh Chung said the report "shows that the PLA is accelerating preparations for a potential armed invasion of Taiwan," even as near-term capability gaps persist.
